words: the built-in tools a kernel seeds on the shelf at light and probes by describe — their DECLARATIONS only (name · words · input schema · consequence class · the ground and master flags · which arguments hold at the interlock), read by both kernels (P7 sp8 row 2). A tool's EXECUTION stays body-side: the Python body binds each name to its executor and refuses to start when a declaration has none; the kernel authorizes, journals and meters, it never runs the call. MCP-born tools never live here — their server lists them onto the shelf.

tools.name: weather
tools.description: Read the real temperature outside right now. Call it with NO arguments to use the operator's own town (the default) — never ask the human where they are first.

tools.name: acquire
tools.description: Acquire a text into your memory under a short key: every word is kept exactly, with its provenance, and the human can recall every word later — by key, by ask, or by timeframe. Use it when the human asks you to remember, keep, acquire, or take in a text.

tools.name: mark
tools.description: Set a marker on what you are executing: a declared kind (e.g. 'improvement') and a short note. Other bodies that declared interest in that kind will be asked to act on it. A kind must be declared first.

tools.name: purge-memory
tools.description: Permanently erase a memory you acquired, every version of it, under a key — the words leave the Record, the projection, and every digest that cited them; only a tombstone with the hashes remains. This cannot be undone; it holds for the human's yes.

tools.name: add-watch
tools.description: Propose a new monitoring watch: a named ALERT on one metric (outbox_pending · oldest_outbox_age_s · asks_received · bodies_alive · bodies_dormant · door_p95_ms — the slowest door's p95 in milliseconds · pool_busy · pool_waiting — the ground pool's strain) — the watch turns RED when `metric op threshold` holds and is green otherwise (ops: <= >= < > ==). To catch dormant bodies: bodies_dormant > 0. To catch asks left waiting: asks_received > 0. To catch a slow door: door_p95_ms > 1000. It holds for the human's yes before it lands. When the human asks you to propose a watch, call this tool — never describe the watch in words instead.

tools.name: draft
tools.description: Save a DRAFT of a craft under the human whose ask you serve — a template, prompt, skill, policy, graph, binding or golden set (Phase 8 sp3, THE WORKSHOP). Routine: a draft is unversioned and lives under the human's seat alone, never on the shelf. Pass the WHOLE declaration as `body` (the full object as it should stand after the change — never a fragment), the draft's `name` (short, lowercase) and its `kind`; the same name and kind updates the human's existing draft. `bench` names the open bench the draft files on — the agent's name (THE STUDIO sp11: a bench is one effort, one place); a draft with no bench is loose. The cut onto the shelf is the human's alone ("cut the <name> draft") — never offer to cut. When the human asks you to change, add to or write a draft, CALL this tool; never describe the change instead.

tools.name: bench
tools.description: Keep THE BENCH — one effort, one place — under the human whose ask you serve (THE STUDIO sp11, THE AGENT MAKES IT ALL). action=open opens a bench named for the agent (`name`, short and lowercase), or hands back the open one of that name. action=read reads what stands on it: its step, its drafts and whether each reads whole, its experiments. action=work files ONE held act — "put <name> to work": the kernel cuts what changed on the bench in order (the graph, the golden set, then the template), skips what already stands, and opens THE EXPERIMENT on the agent's cut; it holds at the interlock for the human's single Yes in the chat, and you never answer it; it refuses in words before any hold when the bench is not whole (no graph, no golden set, no template, nothing changed, an experiment already running). action=close lets the bench go: its drafts discarded, its open experiment declined; what reached the shelf stays. Routine: a bench is the human's own place; the consequential act — the chain — is the kernel's, held at L2 for the human. When the human asks you to make an agent, open its bench, file every draft on it, then call action=work; never describe the act instead.

tools.name: propose
tools.description: Propose a change to a BODY's craft — a DRAFT saved under that body's OWNER, marked with the improvement it came from (Phase 8 sp5, THE OPERATING STATE: the improvement loop closes in the Workshop). Routine: a draft is unversioned and lives under the owner's seat alone, never on the shelf; raw feedback never reaches a body — a proposal does. Pass `for` (the body's name), the WHOLE declaration as `body` (the full object as it should stand after the change — never a fragment), the draft's `name` and `kind` (for a template, `name` is the body's own name — the proposal is its next version, never a new body), and `words` (one line: what changes and why). The owner opens it in the Workshop and cuts it; the Experiment judges it. Never offer to cut; never change anything yourself.

tools.name: services
tools.description: Keep the shelf of services. action=register adds an MCP server (name: a short lowercase name; locator: its command line or URL, or env:NAME; secrets_with: the env NAMES it needs) and lists its tools onto the shelf. action=check probes one service by name, or every MCP server when no name is given. action=retire / restore move a service by name. action=changes reads what changed on the shelf since the last ask. action=list names what stands. Register, retire and restore hold for the human's yes at the interlock; check, changes and list run at once. When the human asks you to add, check, retire or restore, CALL this tool — never describe the act instead.

tools.name: minds
tools.description: Keep the Stable of minds. action=register adds a mind (name: a short lowercase name; provider: anthropic | openrouter | ollama | openai | compatible; model: the model id). Everything else has a default — NEVER ask the human for it: base is only for compatible (ollama reaches the laptop's own Ollama by default); klass defaults to standard (fast | standard | deep); the key is the provider's env NAME by default — never a value; prices are read from the gateway. With a name, a provider and a model in hand, CALL register at once — the hold at the interlock is the human's yes. action=check probes one mind by name or every mind. action=search finds minds (q, klass, max_in_per_m, modality); action=list names what stands. action=assign points a body (subject: its name, or * for every body) at a mind (stall) for a class of work (klass: fast | standard | deep, or any for all its work — the default); action=unassign lifts it. action=fuel reads a body's allowance and spend (subject); action=refill adds dollars (subject, usd). action=spend rolls the meter up. action=retire / restore move a mind by name; action=repin re-pins a mind whose deal moved. action=changes reads what changed. Register, assign, unassign, refill, retire, restore and repin hold for the human's yes at the interlock; the rest run at once. When the human asks you to add, check, assign, refill, retire or restore, CALL this tool — never describe the act instead.

tools.name: seal-record
tools.description: Permanently seal a note so it can never be edited again. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: erase-record
tools.description: Permanently erase a sealed note — every trace of it. This is grave and cannot be undone.
